name: Altrad
verdict: The Altrad group is a privately held French industrial group controlled by its founder and chairman Mohed Altrad (96.95% of the shares). Its UK engineering subsidiary Altrad Babcock admitted health and safety failures and was fined £967,500 at Kirkcaldy Sheriff Court in November 2025 after a metal coil fell on a rigger, leaving him with three skull fractures and a broken shoulder.

why.text: Altrad's money on the All Blacks shirt belongs to the Altrad group, a private company controlled by its founder Mohed Altrad (96.95% of the shares). The group's UK engineering subsidiary Altrad Babcock admitted health and safety failures after a 130kg metal coil fell on rigger Darren Spagnoletta at the Mossmorran plant in Fife, leaving him with three skull fractures and a broken shoulder; in November 2025 Kirkcaldy Sheriff Court fined the firm £900,000 plus a £67,500 victim surcharge, with the sheriff rating its culpability 'high'.
why.messageLine: Altrad's UK subsidiary Altrad Babcock admitted health and safety failures that left a rigger with three skull fractures, and was fined £967,500 by a Scottish court in November 2025.

note: Rating note: propose 'concern' (the company itself has a human-rights finding: a court conviction over serious worker injuries, METHOD.md 'by the company itself'). The link: the group is family-owned, Mohed Altrad 96.95% (Altrad Annual Report 2025; Forbes 2015 profile: 'he owns 80% of the company'), and Altrad Babcock has been part of the group since the September 2022 Doosan Babcock acquisition (Altrad announcement; ScaffMag). The record: Altrad Babcock's guilty plea to health and safety breaches and the £967,500 Kirkcaldy Sheriff Court fine over the Mossmorran incident, two independent publishers (BBC, 5 Nov 2025; The National, 4 Nov 2025). Front of jersey: ALTRAD has been the Official Front of Jersey Sponsor of NZR's Teams in Black since the 2022 six-year deal, and the white ALTRAD mark sits centred on the 2026 'Greatest Rivalry' home jersey. Not counted under METHOD.md: Mohed Altrad's December 2022 French conviction in the FFR/rugby sponsorship case (bribery/misuse of corporate assets — financial) and the June 2026 French tax-fraud investigation (financial); Le Monde's 2020 investigation into migrant workers on Altrad projects in the Gulf is named press, not a court, regulator, UN or NGO finding.
